title: Act on Local Government Subsidy Management
full_text:
CHAPTER 1 GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to ensure transparent and proper management of local government subsidy budgets, including their efficient preparation and execution, by prescribing basic matters concerning the preparation of such budgets, applications and decisions for grants, and use of subsidies.

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act mean the following:
1. "Local government subsidy" means a subsidy or similar payment granted by a local government pursuant to statutes or municipal ordinances to promote or support affairs or projects undertaken by another local government, a corporation, organization, individual, or other person. However, capital investments, contributions, and subsidies granted by a local government from national subsidy resources are excluded.
2. "Local government subsidized project" means a project or affair for which a local government subsidy is disbursed or granted.
3. "Local government subsidized operator" means a person undertaking a local government subsidized project.
4. "Local government subsidy recipient" means a person receiving a local government subsidy from a local government or a local government subsidized operator.

Article 3 (Relationship to Other Acts)
① Except as otherwise provided in other Acts, the management of local government subsidy budgets, including their preparation and execution, shall be governed by this Act.
② Except as specifically provided in this Act, the protection of personal information shall be governed by the Personal Information Protection Act.
③ In applying this Act to matters concerning education, science, and sports or to the special account for educational expenses, "head of a local government" or "Mayor/Do Governor" shall be construed as "superintendent of education," and "Minister of the Interior and Safety" as "Minister of Education."

CHAPTER 2 PREPARATION OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT SUBSIDY BUDGETS

Article 4 (Standard Subsidy Rates for City/Do Funds)
① Projects eligible for local government subsidy payments, categories of expenses, subsidy rates, and amounts shall be determined annually in the budget. For subsidies to other local governments, the standard subsidy rate applicable to each local government subsidized project when applying for budget appropriations and preparing the budget shall be prescribed by ordinance of the Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Do, or Special Self-Governing Province. However, expenses borne by local governments under Article 22 of the Local Finance Act are excluded.
② The head of a local government shall appropriate the share under paragraph 1 in the budget for the relevant fiscal year in preference to other projects.

Article 5 (Applications for Budget Appropriations by Persons Intending to Undertake Local Government Subsidized Projects)
① A person intending to undertake a local government subsidized project shall annually apply to the head of the local government for a budget appropriation for the local government subsidy.
② Even without an application under paragraph 1, the head of a local government may appropriate the necessary subsidy in cases prescribed by municipal ordinance where unavoidable for the local government's policies.
③ An application under paragraph 1 shall be submitted with accompanying documents and shall state the purpose and details of the project, the expenses required, and other necessary matters.
④ Necessary matters concerning applications under paragraphs 1 through 3, including application forms, accompanying documents, and submission dates, shall be determined by the head of the local government.

Article 6 (Preparation and Operation of Local Government Subsidy Budgets)
① The head of a local government shall budget local government subsidies in consideration of the nature of each project, the operator's ability to bear costs, and other relevant factors.
② The head of a local government shall not grant local government subsidies for operating expenses unless expressly authorized by statutes. Categories of expenses that may be used as operating expenses shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ The head of a local government shall systematically manage assistance histories and other relevant information to prevent duplicate grants or grants to ineligible persons.

Article 6-2 (Notification of Budgets Concerning Local Government Subsidies)
① Where the head of a local government submits to the local council a budget bill containing grants of local government subsidies to another local government, the head shall immediately notify the head of the recipient local government of the relevant subsidy budget details, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
② Where the local council adopts the subsidy budget bill under paragraph 1, the head shall immediately notify the head of the recipient local government of the adopted details, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ Notifications under paragraphs 1 and 2 shall be made through the integrated local government subsidy management network under Article 28(1).

CHAPTER 3 PROCEDURES FOR GRANTING LOCAL GOVERNMENT SUBSIDIES

Article 7 (Applications for Local Government Subsidy Grants)
① A person seeking a local government subsidy grant shall, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, submit to the head of the local government, within the time specified by the head, an application stating the purpose and details of the project, its expenses, and other necessary matters, together with a detailed project plan and documents specified by the head. <Amended April 11, 2023>
② The head of a local government shall receive grant applications under paragraph 1 through a public invitation procedure. However, this shall not apply in any of the following cases:
1. A statute or municipal ordinance prescribes a different method for selecting assistance recipients;
2. The recipient of a nationally subsidized project is designated;
3. The donation has a designated purpose;
4. The project was included in the budget upon application by a person intending to undertake it, and its purpose is considered unattainable unless that applicant undertakes it;
5. The person intending to undertake the project is the head of a local government;
6. In addition to cases under subparagraphs 1 through 5, public invitation is considered inappropriate because of a natural disaster or other unavoidable cause.

Article 8 (Decisions to Grant Local Government Subsidies)
① Upon submission of an application under Article 7, the head of a local government shall examine the following matters and decide without delay whether to grant the subsidy:
1. Compliance with statutes, municipal ordinances, and the purpose of the budget;
2. Appropriateness of the project's details;
3. Whether there are errors in calculating the amount;
4. Ability to contribute the applicant's own funds, where the operator bears part of the funding.
② Where applications are received through public invitation under Article 7(2), the head shall obtain deliberation by the Local Government Subsidy Management Committee under Article 26 before deciding whether to grant subsidies under paragraph 1.

Article 9 (Conditions for Local Government Subsidy Grants)
① When deciding to grant a subsidy, the head of a local government may attach conditions necessary to achieve the grant's purpose as prescribed in statutes, municipal ordinances, and the budget.
② When deciding to grant a subsidy, the head may attach a condition requiring the operator, if substantial profits arise upon completion of the project, to return all or part of the subsidy already granted to the local government, insofar as this does not conflict with the purpose of the grant.

Article 10 (Notification of Decisions to Grant Local Government Subsidies) Upon deciding to grant a subsidy, the head of a local government shall notify the applicant without delay of the details of the grant decision, including any conditions attached thereto; the same shall apply hereinafter.

Article 10-2 (Methods of Granting Local Government Subsidies)
① Where considered necessary for efficient execution and management, the head of a local government may deposit local government subsidies in the local government's treasury and grant them to operators.
② Necessary matters concerning the scope of subsidies deposited under paragraph 1, deposit methods, and grant procedures shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 11 (Revocation of Grant Decisions Due to Changed Circumstances)
① After deciding to grant a local government subsidy, the head of a local government may amend the details of the decision or revoke all or part of it if changes in circumstances arising afterward make this particularly necessary. However, this shall not apply to portions of the subsidized project already performed.
② Grounds for revocation under paragraph 1 shall be limited to cases in which a natural disaster or other change in circumstances occurring after the grant decision eliminates the need to continue all or part of the project, and cases prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ A head of a Si, Gun, or autonomous Gu (hereinafter "head of a Si/Gun/Gu") seeking an amendment to, or requesting revocation of, a grant decision for a City/Do subsidy shall submit a document stating the following matters to the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayor, Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Do Governor, or Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter "Mayor/Do Governor"):
1. Grounds requiring revocation or other action regarding the grant decision;
2. The relevant operator's opinion on such revocation or other action;
3. A plan for future use of subsidies not yet granted as a result of revocation.
④ Where a grant decision is revoked under paragraph 1, the head shall grant subsidies, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, for affairs or projects that become particularly necessary because of the revocation.
⑤ Article 10 shall apply mutatis mutandis to amendments to or revocations of grant decisions under paragraph 1.

Article 12 (Revocation of Grant Decisions Due to Violations of Statutes)
① The head of a local government may revoke all or part of a subsidy grant decision where the operator falls under any of the following:
1. Using the subsidy for another purpose;
2. Violating statutes, municipal ordinances, the details of the grant decision, or a disposition by the head under statutes;
3. Receiving the subsidy through a false application or other improper means;
4. Other grounds prescribed by municipal ordinance where performance of the project is difficult.
② Article 10 shall apply mutatis mutandis where a grant decision is revoked under paragraph 1.

CHAPTER 4 PERFORMANCE OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT SUBSIDIZED PROJECTS

Article 13 (Prohibition of Use of Subsidies for Other Purposes) A local government subsidized operator shall perform the project with the care of a good manager in accordance with statutes, the details of the subsidy grant decision, or a disposition by the head of the local government under statutes, and shall not use the subsidy for another purpose.

Article 14 (Changes to Project Details) An operator seeking to change project details or the allocation of project expenses because of changed circumstances shall obtain approval from the head of the local government. However, this shall not apply to minor changes to details or allocations of expenses specified by the head.

Article 15 (Transfer of Projects) An operator seeking, because of changed circumstances, to transfer the project to another operator, suspend it, or discontinue it shall obtain prior approval from the head of the local government.

Article 16 (Checking the Status of Project Performance)
① An operator shall report the status of project performance to the head of the local government as prescribed by the head.
② The head may conduct an on-site investigation where necessary to ascertain the status of project performance.
③ An operator shall retain materials concerning project performance for five years; other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
④ Where the head considers that an operator is not performing the project in accordance with statutes, the details of the grant decision, or a disposition by the head under statutes, the head may issue orders necessary for project performance.
⑤ Where an operator violates an order under paragraph 4, the head may temporarily suspend project performance.

Article 17 (Reports on Project Performance)
① In any of the following cases, an operator shall prepare a report on the performance of the project (hereinafter "performance report") and submit it to the head of the local government by the deadline prescribed by Presidential Decree. The report shall include a settlement report clearly identifying project expenses by funding source and documents specified by the head. However, where the operator has reported performance under Article 27 of the Subsidy Management Act and there is a ground prescribed by Presidential Decree, performance reporting under this Act may be deemed completed:
1. When the project is completed;
2. When approval to discontinue the project is obtained;
3. When the fiscal year ends.
② An operator whose total local government subsidies for the project are at least 300 million won, excluding a local government acting as operator, shall have the appropriateness of its settlement report verified by an auditor under Articles 2, subparagraph 7, and 9 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc. However, this shall not apply where a person undertaking a subsidized or indirectly subsidized project that includes the details of the local government subsidized project has already had the appropriateness of the settlement report verified pursuant to the latter part of Article 27(2) of the Subsidy Management Act. <Amended April 11, 2023>
③ If an operator fails to submit a performance report by the deadline under the former part of paragraph 1, the head may reduce local government subsidies in accordance with criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree, taking account of the period of delay. The reduction shall not exceed 50 percent of the subsidy first granted after submission of the performance report. <Added April 11, 2023>
④ Necessary matters concerning submission of performance reports and verification of settlement reports under paragraphs 1 and 2 shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended April 11, 2023>

Article 18 (Accounting Audits of Specified Local Government Subsidized Operators)
① An operator receiving total local government subsidies of at least one billion won from the head of a local government during the same fiscal year, excluding a local government acting as operator (hereinafter in this Article "specified local government subsidized operator"), shall submit to the head granting the subsidies an audit report prepared for that fiscal year by an auditor under Articles 2, subparagraph 7, and 9 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc. (hereinafter in this Article "audit report"). However, a specified operator receiving subsidies for at least two consecutive years that submitted an audit report for the immediately preceding fiscal year may omit preparation and submission of an audit report for the relevant fiscal year.
② Notwithstanding paragraph 1, a specified operator subject to an accounting audit under another Act may submit an audit-related report prepared under that Act in place of the audit report. The audit-related report shall include an audit opinion on the local government subsidized project.
③ Notwithstanding paragraphs 1 and 2, where the head considers preparation and submission of an audit report inappropriate in view of the nature of the project, the head may exempt the specified operator from submitting it.
④ In addition to paragraphs 1 through 3, necessary matters concerning selection of auditors by specified operators, accounting audit standards, and preparation and submission of audit reports shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 19 (Finalization of Subsidy Amounts)
① On the basis of a performance report prepared by an operator under Article 17, the head of a local government shall examine whether the project complies with statutes, municipal ordinances, the details of the grant decision, or a disposition by the head under statutes. An on-site investigation may be conducted where necessary.
② If the examination under paragraph 1 finds compliance, the head shall finalize the subsidy amount and notify the operator.

Article 20 (Orders to Correct Local Government Subsidized Projects) Upon receiving a performance report, if the head of a local government considers that project performance does not comply with statutes, municipal ordinances, the details of the grant decision, or a disposition by the head under statutes, the head may order the operator to take measures necessary to correct the project.

Article 20-2 (Disclosure of Information by Local Government Subsidized Operators)
① Upon the end of each fiscal year, an operator undertaking a project of at least the scale prescribed by Presidential Decree, excluding a local government, shall disclose the following documents through the integrated local government subsidy management network under Article 28(1) by the deadline prescribed by Presidential Decree. However, this shall not apply where a person undertaking a subsidized or indirectly subsidized project that includes the details of the local government subsidized project has already made disclosure under Article 26-10(1) of the Subsidy Management Act:
1. The grant application and accompanying documents under Article 7(1);
2. The settlement report on project expenses under the latter part of Article 17(1);
3. Where an audit was conducted under Article 18(1) or (2), the audit report or audit-related report;
4. Where the project was audited by the Board of Audit and Inspection, a central administrative agency, a local government, or other relevant body, documents concerning the audit results;
5. Other important documents concerning project performance prescribed by Presidential Decree.
② The head of a local government may, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, issue a corrective order, reduce subsidies, or take measures necessary therefor against an operator that fails to disclose information by the deadline under the main clause of paragraph 1 or discloses false facts. The reduction shall not exceed 50 percent of total subsidies scheduled to be granted in the fiscal year for which disclosure is made under paragraph 1.

Article 21 (Restrictions on Disposal of Property)
① An operator shall, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, clearly identify the current value and increases and decreases of important property acquired or improved in utility through local government subsidies and prescribed by Presidential Decree (hereinafter "important property"), and report its status to the head of the local government.
② Upon receiving a report on important property under paragraph 1, the head shall disclose the reported status as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added April 11, 2023>
③ Even after completion of the project, an operator shall not undertake any of the following regarding important property without approval from the head of the local government: <Amended April 11, 2023>
1. Use for purposes other than the purpose of the grant;
2. Transfer, exchange, or lease;
3. Provision as collateral.
④ In any of the following cases, an operator may undertake the acts in the subparagraphs of paragraph 3 without approval from the head: <Amended April 11, 2023>
1. The operator has returned the entire subsidy to the local government;
2. The period specified by the head in consideration of the purpose of the subsidy grant and the property's useful life has elapsed;
3. Other grounds prescribed by Presidential Decree arise.
⑤ Where, even after completion of the project, an operator undertakes an act in any subparagraph of paragraph 2 regarding important property without approval from the head, the head may, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, order return of all or part of the following amounts: <Amended April 11, 2023>
1. An amount corresponding to the subsidy used to acquire the important property;
2. An amount corresponding to the increase in the property's utility value;
3. An amount corresponding to the financial benefits obtained by transferring, exchanging, leasing, or providing the property as collateral.

Article 22 (Supplementary Registration of Important Property)
① When registering ownership of real estate constituting important property, an operator shall make a supplementary registration indicating the following matters. However, this shall not apply to real estate acquired and managed by a local government under the Public Property and Commodity Management Act or other relevant statutes:
1. That the real estate was acquired through a local government subsidy or its utility value was increased thereby;
2. That approval from the head of the local government is required to use the real estate for another purpose, transfer, exchange, lease, or provide it as collateral within the period specified by the head.
② Supplementary registration under paragraph 1 shall be made simultaneously with registration of ownership preservation, ownership transfer, or changes to the description of land or buildings. However, where the subsidy grant does not alter the registered details of the real estate, supplementary registration shall be made before submission of the performance report.
③ If, after the date of supplementary registration under paragraph 1, important property is used for another purpose, transferred, exchanged, leased, or provided as collateral in violation of Article 21(3), such acts shall be void. <Amended April 11, 2023>
④ An operator may cancel the supplementary registration under paragraph 1 in any of the following cases:
1. The operator has returned the entire subsidy to the local government under Article 9(2) or 31, and the head has confirmed that fact;
2. The period specified by the head in consideration of the purpose of the grant and the real estate's useful life has elapsed.

CHAPTER 5 MANAGEMENT OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT SUBSIDIES

Article 23 Deleted. <April 11, 2023>

Article 24 (Establishment of Separate Accounts)
① An operator shall establish a separate account for subsidies granted and account for them distinctly from its own receipts and disbursements.
② Where the operator is the head of a Si/Gun/Gu, accounting under paragraph 1 shall distinguish the expenses of the City/Do and Si/Gun/Gu required to execute the project and their respective execution results.

Article 25 Deleted. <April 11, 2023>

Article 26 (Local Government Subsidy Management Committee)
① A Local Government Subsidy Management Committee shall be established under the head of a local government to conduct expert deliberation on matters concerning local government subsidies.
② The head shall obtain deliberation by the Committee in advance in any of the following cases. However, deliberation may be omitted in cases prescribed by Presidential Decree: <Amended April 11, 2023>
1. Preparing a local government subsidy budget;
2. Submitting a bill for a municipal ordinance concerning subsidies to the local council;
3. Deciding matters concerning the sharing of project funding between subsidies and operators;
4. Paying reporting rewards under Article 36-3;
5. When an operational evaluation of a project under Article 27 has been conducted;
6. Whether to publish a list under Article 30(1);
7. Other cases prescribed by municipal ordinance as necessary for subsidy management.
③ The Committee under paragraph 1 shall consist of no more than 15 members, including one chairperson, with consideration given to gender.
④ Members under paragraph 3 shall be appointed or commissioned from civilian members, including faculty of national and public schools under the Higher Education Act, and public officials, meaning general service officials under Article 2(2)1 of the Local Public Officials Act. Public official members shall not exceed one fourth of the total.
⑤ The chairperson shall be elected from among the civilian members.
⑥ The term of civilian members shall be prescribed by municipal ordinance within three years, and may be renewed only once.
⑦ A member shall be excluded from deliberation on an agenda item in either of the following cases:
1. The member or a person related to the member has an interest in the agenda item;
2. The institution to which the member belongs has an interest in the item, such as providing services or advice concerning it.
⑧ A party to an agenda item before the Committee may request recusal of a member where circumstances make fair deliberation difficult to expect, and the Committee shall decide by resolution. The challenged member shall not participate in that resolution.
⑨ A member falling under a ground for exclusion in any subparagraph of paragraph 7 shall voluntarily abstain from deliberation on the relevant item.
⑩ The head of a local government may dismiss or discharge a member in any of the following cases:
1. The member becomes unable to perform duties because of physical or mental disability;
2. Misconduct related to the member's duties is found;
3. Continued membership is considered inappropriate because of neglect of duties, damage to dignity, or another reason;
4. The member expresses difficulty in performing duties.
⑪ A meeting of the Committee shall open with a majority of incumbent members present, and resolutions shall require the approval of a majority of members present.
⑫ Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Committee other than those in paragraphs 1 through 11 shall be prescribed by municipal ordinance.

Article 27 (Operational Evaluation of Local Government Subsidized Projects)
① The head of a local government shall evaluate project performance annually and, absent special grounds, reflect the results in budget preparation. However, nationally subsidized projects may be excepted.
② For continuing projects, the head shall evaluate every three years the need to maintain them and, following deliberation by the Committee, take necessary measures according to the evaluation results.

Article 28 (Establishment and Operation of the Integrated Local Government Subsidy Management Network)
① The Minister of the Interior and Safety and heads of local governments shall establish and operate an integrated local government subsidy management network (hereinafter "integrated local government subsidy management network") to facilitate project performance and prevent duplicate or improper receipt of subsidies.
② The network shall include materials or information concerning the following matters (hereinafter "local government subsidy management information"):
1. Assistance histories under Article 6(3);
2. Applications for grants under Article 7;
3. Grant decisions under Article 8;
4. Project performance status under Article 16(1) and on-site investigations under paragraph 2 of that Article;
5. Operators' performance reports under Article 17(1) and verification of settlement reports under paragraph 2 of that Article;
6. Status of important property under Article 21(1);
7. Project performance evaluations under Article 27(1) and measures under paragraph 2 of that Article;
8. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree for efficient execution and management of subsidies and projects.
③ Where considered necessary for efficient execution and management, the Minister may request heads of relevant institutions to link the network with the following information systems. A head receiving a request shall comply unless there are special grounds:
1. The integrated information computer network under Article 15-5(1) of the Framework Act on Employment Policy;
2. The vocational skills development information network under Article 6(1) of the National Lifelong Vocational Skills Development Act;
3. The integrated subsidy management network under Article 26-2(1) of the Subsidy Management Act;
4. The social security information system under Article 37(2) of the Framework Act on Social Security;
5. The information system under Article 6-2(1) of the Social Welfare Services Act;
6. The social services electronic voucher management system under Article 28(1) of the Act on the Use of Social Services and Management of Vouchers;
7. The integrated child care information system under Article 9-3(1) of the Child Care Act;
8. The early childhood education information system under Article 19-2(1) of the Early Childhood Education Act;
9. The education information system under Article 30-4(1) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act;
10. Other information systems prescribed by Presidential Decree as necessary for efficient execution and management of subsidies and projects.
④ Where considered necessary to check duplicate or improper receipt or execution details of subsidies, the Minister and heads of local governments may collect and process subsidy-related materials or information by linking the network with other information systems in the subparagraphs of paragraph 3. "Process" means processing under Article 2, subparagraph 2, of the Personal Information Protection Act; the same applies in Articles 28-2 through 28-4 and 36-5.

Article 28-2 (Requests for Materials or Information)
① Where considered necessary for efficient execution and management of subsidies and projects, including selection and eligibility management of operators or subsidy recipients (hereinafter "operators, etc.") and prevention of duplicate or improper receipt, the Minister of the Interior and Safety and heads of local governments may request heads of relevant institutions to provide the following materials or information. A head shall comply unless there are special grounds:
1. Computerized information on registered family relationship matters under Article 9 of the Act on Registration of Family Relations;
2. Registration records under the Registration of Real Estate Act;
3. Computerized resident registration information under Article 30 of the Resident Registration Act;
4. The following tax-related materials or information:
(a) Information prescribed by Presidential Decree among taxation information under Article 81-13(1) of the Framework Act on National Taxes;
(b) Tax payment certificates under Article 108 of the National Tax Collection Act;
(c) Materials or information on business registration under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act;
(d) Electronic tax invoices or corrected electronic tax invoices under Article 32(2) and (7) of the Value-Added Tax Act;
(e) Electronic invoices under the latter part of Article 163(1) of the Income Tax Act;
(f) Materials or information prescribed by Presidential Decree among taxation information or taxation materials under Articles 86(1) and 132 of the Framework Act on Local Taxes;
(g) Tax payment certificates under Article 5 of the Local Tax Collection Act;
5. Materials or information concerning the following insurance, pensions, and benefits:
(a) National health insurance under the National Health Insurance Act;
(b) National basic livelihood security benefits under the National Basic Living Security Act;
(c) National pensions under the National Pension Act;
(d) Employment insurance under the Employment Insurance Act;
(e) Basic pensions under the Basic Pension Act;
(f) Industrial accident compensation insurance under the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act;
(g) Pensions for persons with disabilities under the Act on Pensions for Persons with Disabilities;
6. Other materials or information prescribed by Presidential Decree for efficient execution and management of subsidies and projects.
② Where considered necessary for efficient analysis and management of materials or information provided under paragraph 1, the Minister and heads of local governments may process them through the integrated local government subsidy management network.
③ Matters necessary for requesting materials or information from relevant institutions and processing them, other than those in paragraphs 1 and 2, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 28-3 (Requests for Financial or Credit Information)
① Notwithstanding Article 4(1) of the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality and Article 32(2) of the Credit Information Use and Protection Act, the Minister of the Interior and Safety and heads of local governments may receive and process the following materials or information from heads of financial institutions, etc., to the extent necessary for efficient execution and management of subsidies and projects, including selection and eligibility management of operators, etc., and prevention of duplicate or improper receipt. "Financial institutions, etc." means financial companies, etc., under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality and credit information concentration institutions under Article 25 of the Credit Information Use and Protection Act; the same applies throughout this Article. The Minister and heads may receive and process such materials or information through the integrated local government subsidy management network:
1. Materials or information on financial assets and financial transactions under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality (hereinafter "financial information");
2. Credit information under the Credit Information Use and Protection Act (hereinafter "credit information").
② When requesting financial or credit information from heads of financial institutions, etc., under paragraph 1, the Minister and heads of local governments shall also submit written consent to provision of information from the person in whose name the information is held. Such written consent may be converted to electronic form for submission.
③ A head of a financial institution, etc., receiving a request under paragraph 1 shall provide the financial or credit information notwithstanding Article 4 of the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality and Article 32 of the Credit Information Use and Protection Act.
④ A head providing financial or credit information under paragraph 3 shall notify the person in whose name it is held of that provision. However, where that person consented in advance, notification may be omitted notwithstanding Article 4-2(1) of the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality and Article 32(7) of the Credit Information Use and Protection Act.
⑤ Matters necessary for requests and processing, consent of the person in whose name information is held, and notification to that person, other than those in paragraphs 1 through 4, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 28-4 (Protection of Subsidy Management Information)
① The Minister of the Interior and Safety and heads of local governments shall use the following materials or information (hereinafter in this Article "subsidy management information, etc.") only to the extent necessary for efficient execution and management of subsidies and projects, and shall establish and implement policies or measures necessary for their secure protection:
1. Local government subsidy management information;
2. Materials or information collected under Article 28(4);
3. Materials or information provided under Article 28-2;
4. Financial or credit information provided under Article 28-3.
② No person shall engage in any of the following acts concerning subsidy management information, etc., or the integrated local government subsidy management network:
1. Forging, altering, damaging, or deleting subsidy management information, etc., with intent to obstruct its processing;
2. Using information learned in the course of duties for another purpose, or providing or divulging it to a third party;
3. Altering or damaging the network without legitimate authority;
4. Processing subsidy management information, etc., without legitimate authority or beyond permitted authority.
③ Notwithstanding paragraph 2, subparagraph 2, the Minister may provide subsidy management information, etc., to a third party for use for another purpose in any of the following cases. However, in the case of subparagraph 1, approval from the Minister shall be obtained for such other use:
1. Separate consent to provision of the information has been obtained from the data subject under Article 2, subparagraph 3, of the Personal Information Protection Act;
2. The information is requested pursuant to a court order to submit it or a warrant issued by a judge;
3. Another Act specifically provides for provision and use of the information.

Article 28-5 (Destruction of Subsidy Management Information)
① The Minister of the Interior and Safety and heads of local governments holding subsidy management information shall immediately destroy it five years after the date it was first held. However, materials or information prescribed by Presidential Decree whose continued retention is considered necessary to prevent duplicate or improper receipt of subsidies may be retained beyond five years until the deadline for which the necessity is recognized.
② Where the Minister and heads hold materials or information under Article 28(4), 28-2(1), or 28-3(1), they shall destroy them immediately upon achieving the purpose of retention. However, where preservation is required by other statutes or they are needed as evidence for litigation, investigation, audit, or similar proceedings, continued retention is permitted as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 29 (Inspection)
① Where considered necessary to ensure proper execution of subsidy budgets, the head of a local government may require an operator to report, have public officials under the head inspect books, documents, or other property at the operator's office or place of business, or have them question relevant persons.
② A public official conducting an inspection or questioning under paragraph 1 shall carry proof of authority and present it to relevant persons.

Article 30 (Publication of Lists)
① By March 31 each year, the head of a local government shall publish on the local government's website a list of persons falling under any of the following and matters prescribed by Presidential Decree concerning their dispositions, including violations and details of dispositions: <Amended April 11, 2023>
1. An operator that has received a corrective order or subsidy reduction under the former part of Article 20-2(2) at least three times;
2. An operator falling under any subparagraph of Article 32(1);
3. A subsidy recipient falling under any subparagraph of Article 32(3).
② Notwithstanding paragraph 1, the head may omit publication where there are grounds prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the death of the person making publication ineffective or publication being inappropriate.
③ Before publication under paragraph 1, the head shall notify the person concerned and provide an opportunity to submit explanatory materials or state an opinion.
④ Where an objection under Article 36-2 or another challenge procedure is pending concerning revocation of a grant decision, an order to return subsidies, or other relevant disposition, the head shall publish under paragraph 1 after the challenge procedure has concluded. <Amended April 11, 2023>
⑤ Necessary matters concerning methods and procedures of publication, other than those in paragraphs 1 through 4, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER 6 RETURN OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT SUBSIDIES AND SANCTIONS

Article 31 (Return of Local Government Subsidies)
① Where a grant decision is revoked and subsidies have already been granted for the revoked portion of the project, the head of the local government shall set a deadline and order return of the corresponding subsidy and interest generated thereby.
② Where the head finalizes the subsidy amount payable to an operator under Article 19(2), and the amount already granted plus interest generated thereby exceeds the finalized amount, the head shall set a deadline and order return of the excess. However, where the operator is the head of a local government, this shall not apply to interest generated after receipt of the subsidy because of unavoidable grounds prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 32 (Exclusion from Performance of Subsidized Projects)
① Where an operator falls under any of the following, the head of a local government shall exclude the operator from performing projects under the head's jurisdiction or restrict subsidy grants for a period not exceeding five years, as prescribed by Presidential Decree: <Amended April 11, 2023>
1. All or part of a grant decision has been revoked at least once under Article 12 because the operator obtained subsidies through deception or other improper means;
2. All or part of a grant decision has been revoked at least twice under Article 12 because the operator used subsidies for another purpose;
3. All or part of a grant decision has been revoked at least three times under Article 12 because the operator violated statutes, municipal ordinances, the details of a grant decision, or a disposition by the head under statutes.
② Notwithstanding paragraph 1, where the project is a welfare project, nationally subsidized project, or other project prescribed by Presidential Decree and replacing the operator is difficult, exclusion or restriction may be omitted following deliberation by the Local Government Subsidy Management Committee. <Added April 11, 2023>
③ Where a subsidy recipient falls under any of the following, the head shall restrict subsidy payments to that recipient for a period not exceeding five years, as prescribed by Presidential Decree: <Amended April 11, 2023>
1. An order to return all or part of subsidies has been issued at least once under Article 34 because the recipient obtained them through deception or other improper means;
2. An order to return all or part of subsidies has been issued at least twice under Article 34 because the recipient used them for a purpose different from that of payment;
3. An order to return all or part of subsidies has been issued at least three times under Article 34 because the recipient obtained them without meeting eligibility requirements.
④ Notwithstanding paragraph 3, the head may omit payment restrictions where the subsidy received falls under any of the following: <Added April 11, 2023>
1. Benefits under Article 7 of the National Basic Living Security Act;
2. Disability allowances under Article 49 of the Act on Welfare of Persons with Disabilities;
3. Basic pensions under the Basic Pension Act;
4. Welfare benefits under Article 12 of the Single-Parent Family Support Act;
5. Other cases prescribed by Presidential Decree where restricting subsidies to the recipient is inappropriate considering the nature and functions of the subsidy.
⑤ The head shall exclude a person whose conviction has become final for obtaining financial benefits by deception or other improper means in the bidding, award, conclusion, or performance of a contract related to a local government subsidized project (hereinafter "improper contracting enterprise") from performing projects under the head's jurisdiction for a period not exceeding five years, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added April 11, 2023>
⑥ Where the head excludes operators, etc., or improper contracting enterprises from project performance or restricts their grant or receipt of subsidies under paragraphs 1 through 5, the head shall immediately notify heads of other local governments. <Amended April 11, 2023>
⑦ Heads of other local governments notified under paragraph 6 shall exclude the relevant operators, etc., from projects under their jurisdiction or restrict their grant or receipt of subsidies. Paragraphs 1 through 5 shall apply mutatis mutandis to criteria for exclusion and its exceptions and restrictions on grant or receipt and their exceptions. <Added April 11, 2023>
⑧ Necessary matters concerning exclusion and restrictions on grant or receipt, other than those in paragraphs 1 through 7, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended April 11, 2023>

Article 33 (Temporary Suspension of Other Subsidy Grants) Where an operator fails to comply with an order to return subsidies and interest under Article 31(1) or (2), and other subsidies are payable to the operator for affairs or projects of the same kind, the head of a local government may temporarily suspend those grants or offset the unpaid amount against those subsidies.

Article 34 (Recovery of Subsidies from Recipients)
① Where a subsidy recipient falls under any of the following, the head of the local government and the operator shall set a deadline and order return of all or part of subsidies paid:
1. Obtaining the subsidy through deception or other improper means;
2. Using the subsidy for a purpose different from that of payment;
3. Being found not to meet the requirements for receiving the subsidy.
② An operator issuing a return order under paragraph 1 shall notify the head of the local government responsible for the project as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ An operator may withhold subsidies for a period specified by the head where the recipient falls under any subparagraph of paragraph 1.
④ The head may order an operator to restrict subsidy payments to a recipient for a specified period where that recipient falls under any subparagraph of paragraph 1.

Article 35 (Imposition and Collection of Sanction Surcharges and Additional Charges)
① In any of the following cases, the head of a local government shall impose and collect a sanction surcharge from operators, etc., not exceeding five times the total subsidies to be returned, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. However, where grounds prescribed by Presidential Decree exist, such as the imposition, before or after the surcharge, of a fine, minor fine, confiscation, additional collection, penalty surcharge, or administrative fine under this or another Act because of improper receipt of subsidies, the surcharge may be exempted, reduced, modified, or revoked: <Amended April 11, 2023>
1. Return of subsidies has been ordered under Article 31(1), limited to revocation of grant decisions under Article 12;
2. An operator has ordered a recipient to return subsidies under Article 34.
② When imposing a surcharge on the ground in paragraph 1, subparagraph 2, the head shall first investigate and confirm the appropriateness of the operator's return order under Article 34.
③ Notwithstanding paragraph 1, a surcharge may be omitted where subsidies fall under any of the following:
1. Benefits under Article 7 of the National Basic Living Security Act;
2. Disability allowances under Article 49 of the Act on Welfare of Persons with Disabilities;
3. Basic pensions under the Basic Pension Act;
4. Welfare benefits under Article 12 of the Single-Parent Family Support Act;
5. Other cases prescribed by Presidential Decree where the practical benefit of imposing and collecting a surcharge is not substantial.
④ Where a person liable for a surcharge under paragraph 1 fails to pay by the deadline, the head may collect an additional charge not exceeding five percent of the overdue amount for the period from the day after the deadline through the day before payment.
⑤ Necessary matters concerning calculation and imposition procedures for surcharges and additional charges, other than those in paragraphs 1 through 4, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 36 (Compulsory Collection)
① The head of a local government may collect return amounts, sanction surcharges, and additional charges according to procedures for disposition of local tax arrears or under the Act on the Collection of Local Administrative Sanctions and Charges, Etc., in the following cases:
1. An operator fails to pay a return amount under Article 21 or 31 by the deadline;
2. A recipient fails to pay a return amount under Article 34 by the deadline;
3. Operators, etc., fail to pay surcharges or additional charges under Article 35 by the deadline.
② Collection under paragraph 1 shall take priority over other public dues and claims, except national and local taxes.

CHAPTER 7 SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS <Added April 11, 2023>

Article 36-2 (Objections)
① An operator objecting to a grant decision, grant conditions, revocation, an order to return or reduce subsidies, exclusion from project performance, restriction on grant or receipt, imposition of a surcharge, or another disposition by the head concerning subsidy grants may file a written objection with the head within 20 days after receiving notification or the disposition.
② A subsidy recipient objecting to a return order or reduction, exclusion from project performance, restriction on grant or receipt, imposition of a surcharge, or another disposition by the head concerning subsidy grants may file a written objection with the head within 20 days after receiving notification or the disposition.
③ Upon receiving an objection under paragraph 1 or 2, the head shall hear the opinions of relevant persons, take necessary measures, and notify the objector. If an objector regarding the details of a grant decision fails to express acceptance within 20 days after receiving that notification, the subsidy grant application shall be deemed withdrawn.

Article 36-3 (Payment of Reporting Rewards)
① The head of a local government may pay a reward within budget limits to a person reporting or filing a complaint with a relevant administrative authority or investigative agency against a person falling under any of the following. However, no reward shall be paid to a public official reporting in relation to official duties:
1. An operator falling under any subparagraph of Article 12(1);
2. A subsidy recipient falling under any subparagraph of Article 34(1).
② Necessary matters concerning criteria and procedures for rewards under paragraph 1 shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 36-4 (Establishment of Online Service Systems) The Minister of the Interior and Safety may establish and operate an online service system where necessary to disclose and provide materials or information on subsidies and projects to the general public.

Article 36-5 (Entrustment of Duties) The Minister and heads of local governments may entrust the following duties to institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree:
1. Operation of the integrated local government subsidy management network;
2. Processing of materials or information in the subparagraphs of Article 28-4(1);
3. Operation of the online service system under Article 36-4.

Article 36-6 (Deeming Persons Public Officials for Application of Penalty Provisions) Officers and employees of institutions engaged in duties entrusted under Article 36-5 who are not public officials shall be deemed public officials when Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act are applied.

CHAPTER 8 PENALTY PROVISIONS <Amended April 11, 2023>

Article 37 (Penalties) A person falling under either of the following shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than ten years or a fine not exceeding 100 million won:
1. A person who obtains a grant or payment of a local government subsidy through a false application or other improper means, or a person who knowingly grants or pays a local government subsidy in such circumstances;
2. A person who violates Article 28-4(2)1.

Article 38 (Penalties) A person falling under any of the following shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than five years or a fine not exceeding 50 million won: <Amended April 11, 2023>
1. A person who uses subsidies for another purpose in violation of Article 13;
2. A person who, in violation of Article 21(3), undertakes a prohibited act concerning important property without approval from the head;
3. A person who violates any of subparagraphs 2 through 4 of Article 28-4(2).

Article 39 (Penalties)
① A person who violates Article 14 or 15 shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than two years or a fine not exceeding 20 million won.
② A person falling under any of the following shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than one year or a fine not exceeding ten million won:
1. A person who fails to retain relevant materials in violation of Article 16(3);
2. A person who violates a suspension order under Article 16(5);
3. A person who makes a false report in violation of Article 17 or 29(1).

Article 40 (Joint Penalty Provisions) Where the representative of a corporation, or an agent, employee, or other worker of a corporation or individual, commits a violation falling under any of Articles 37 through 39 in connection with the business of that corporation or individual, the corporation or individual shall also be punished by the fine prescribed in the relevant Article, in addition to punishment of the offender. However, this shall not apply where the corporation or individual has not neglected reasonable care and supervision concerning the business to prevent the violation.

ADDENDA <Act No. 17892, January 12, 2021>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force six months after the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Transitional Measures Concerning Local Government Subsidy Review Committees)
(1) A Local Government Subsidy Review Committee under Article 32-3 of the former Local Finance Act existing when this Act enters into force shall be deemed a Local Government Subsidy Management Committee under this Act.
(2) A member of a Local Government Subsidy Review Committee appointed or commissioned under Article 32-3 of the former Local Finance Act when this Act enters into force shall be deemed appointed or commissioned as a member of a Local Government Subsidy Management Committee under this Act.

Article 3 (Amendment of Another Act)
The Local Finance Act is partially amended as follows:
Chapter II-2 (Articles 32-2 through 32-11) is deleted.
Article 37-2(2) is amended as follows, and paragraphs (3) through (8) of that Article are newly inserted as follows:
(2) The Local Financial Investment Review Committee under paragraph (1) shall consist of not more than 15 members, including one chairperson, with consideration given to gender.
(3) The members under paragraph (2) shall be appointed or commissioned from among private sector members (including teaching staff of national and public schools under the Higher Education Act) and public officials (meaning public officials in general service under Article 2(2)1 of the Local Public Officials Act), provided that members who are public officials must not exceed one quarter of all members.
(4) The chairperson shall be elected by and from among the private sector members.
(5) The term of office of a private sector member shall be prescribed by municipal ordinance within a period not exceeding three years, and the member may be reappointed only once.
(6) A member shall be excluded from deliberation on an agenda item in any of the following cases:
1. Where the member or a relative of the member has an interest in the agenda item subject to deliberation;
2. Where the institution to which the member belongs has an interest in the agenda item, including by performing services or providing advice related to that item.
(7) Where circumstances make it difficult to expect impartial deliberation by a member, a party to an agenda item subject to deliberation by the Local Financial Investment Review Committee may apply to that Committee for the member's recusal, and the Committee shall decide the matter by resolution. The member concerned must not participate in that resolution.
(8) Where a ground for exclusion under any subparagraph of paragraph (6) applies, a member shall voluntarily refrain from deliberation on the relevant agenda item.
In the former part of Article 60(3), "Article 32-3(2) through" is replaced with "Article 37-2(2) through", and in the latter part of that paragraph, "Local Government Subsidy Review Committee" is replaced with "Local Financial Investment Review Committee".
Articles 97 and 98 are deleted.

Article 4 (Relationship to Other Statutes and Regulations)
Where other statutes and regulations, when this Act enters into force, cite the former Local Finance Act or its provisions regarding the management and operation of local government subsidies, they shall be deemed to cite this Act or the corresponding provisions of this Act in place of the former Local Finance Act or its provisions.

ADDENDA <Act No. 19333, April 11, 2023>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force six months after the date of its promulgation. However, the amended provisions of Articles 10-2, 28, 28-2 through 28-5, 36-4 through 36-6, and 37, and subparagraph 3 of Article 38 shall enter into force on the date of promulgation.

Article 2 (Applicability of Notification of Budget Bills Including Local Government Subsidies)
The amended provisions of Article 6-2 shall apply beginning with budget bills submitted to local councils in the fiscal year following the fiscal year in which this Act enters into force.

Article 3 (Applicability of Reduction of Local Government Subsidies for Delayed Submission of Performance Reports)
The amended provisions of Article 17(3) shall apply beginning with cases where the deadline for submission of a performance report under paragraph (1) of that Article expires after this Act enters into force.

Article 4 (Applicability of Public Disclosure of Information by Local Government Subsidized Operators)
The amended provisions of Article 20-2 shall apply beginning with the fiscal year following the fiscal year in which this Act enters into force.

Article 5 (Applicability of Periods of Exclusion of Local Government Subsidized Operators from Performance of Local Government Subsidized Projects)
(1) The amended introductory provisions of Article 32(1), excluding its subparagraphs, and the amended provisions of paragraph (2) of that Article shall also apply where, before this Act enters into force, a local government subsidized operator falls under any subparagraph of paragraph (1) of that Article and, after this Act enters into force, the operator must be excluded from performing local government subsidized projects or restricted from receiving local government subsidies.
(2) The amended introductory provisions of Article 32(3), excluding its subparagraphs, and the amended provisions of paragraph (4) of that Article shall also apply where, before this Act enters into force, a local government subsidy recipient falls under any subparagraph of paragraph (3) of that Article and, after this Act enters into force, payment of local government subsidies must be restricted.
(3) The amended provisions of Article 32(5) shall apply beginning with cases where a conviction becomes final for a criminal act committed after this Act enters into force.
(4) The amended provisions of Article 32(7) shall also apply where, pursuant to notification by the head of another local government under the former part of paragraph (6) of that Article before this Act enters into force, a local government subsidized operator must be excluded from performing local government subsidized projects or restricted from receiving local government subsidies after this Act enters into force.

Article 6 (Transitional Measures Concerning Verification of Performance Reports)
Where a ground for submission of a performance report under any subparagraph of Article 17(1) arises before this Act enters into force and the deadline for submission under the introductory provisions of that paragraph, excluding its subparagraphs, expires after this Act enters into force, the former provisions of Article 17(2) shall apply notwithstanding the amended proviso to Article 17(2).
